meeting_header: Date: 2026-09-02 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Location: Virtual call (Zoom) | Redwood owner: Ethan Moreno | Attendees: Ethan, Priya (Redwood) — Jordan, Maya, Alvaro (CrescentPay)
summary: Intro demo of Redwood rate limiting, fairshare and org/project key zoning for a payments scale use case. Focus on how to isolate latencies across teams, set burst vs sustained quotas, and map keys to billing/orgs. Security questions on SOC2, KMS, and VPC surfaced; action to send security pack and pilot pricing.
transcript: [00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're gonna keep this pretty practical, walk through how we do rate controls and org/project key zoning. Jordan, Maya, you cool with that?
[00:22] Jordan (CrescentPay CTO): Yep sounds good. We've got a ton of bursty card validation traffic and we want to avoid one product team impacting the rest of the platform.

[00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): Awesome, we'll show the Console first — policy-driven rate slices, then the API mapping and how Optimize suggests batch/quantization changes. Quick note: I'll demo with a test org called crescent-pay-prod but that's just sandbox config.
[01:15] Maya (Infra): Quick ask — we need per-team SLAs and also per-API-key billing tags. Can Redwood support org-level billing attribution?
[01:40] Ethan: Yep, you can map project keys to orgs, and each key carries metadata for billing. In Dedicated you can also get reserved pools per org. We'll show both hosted and dedicated patterns.
[02:05] Alvaro (Product): What about burst capacity — we have spikes during settlement windows where traffic is 5x normal for ~90s. How do you avoid throttling them too harshly?

[02:28] Priya: Great question. We use leaky-bucket style quotas with configurable burst tokens plus fairshare weights. So you can allow short bursts for a key but also set a sustained QPS. It smooths when there's a big spike. Sometimes the console labels the sustained as "sustaind" in the UI — small nit, the value is accurate.
[02:55] Jordan: Is the burst global across org or per-project key?

[03:10] Priya: Configurable. You can allocate bursts per project key, or create an org-level pool that's shared. We also surface token usage and sticky routing so certain keys stick to reserved capacity to guarantee latency.

[03:40] Ethan: I'll share a short policy example — we call it a 'capacity slice' — that has baseline qps 50, burst 300 tokens, fairshare weight 1.5 for payments team so they get priority on contention.
[04:05] [screen share pause — console loading noise]

[04:20] Priya: On the Console: here is the policy editor. You can pick condition rules — header, org id, route prefix — and then attach a quota policy. Note: autocompletion sometimes shows "K-V cache" spelled kv-cache which is fine but the doc spells it differently.
[04:55] Maya: Can we import our existing API keys en masse? We have thousands.
[05:10] Priya: Yes — bulk key import via CSV or API. The import lets you set project -> org mappings and tags like cost center. We'll send an example CSV later.
[05:35] Jordan: How do you handle backpressure when capacity is exhausted? We can't have user-facing timeouts.

[05:52] Priya: Two layers: graceful HTTP 429s with Retry-After for non-critical jobs, and automatic fallback routing to a lower-cost model variant, or to a dedicated reserve if configured. For most infra-critical endpoints you can pin keys to dedicated slices to avoid 429s altogether.
[06:20] Alvaro: Lower-cost variant — do you mean a smaller model? Is that automatic?

[06:35] Priya: Yes, Redwood can route to a compatibile model variant when the preferred model is saturated. Optimize will also suggest quantization profiles; not fully automatic unless you enable policy-based fallback.
[06:58] Jordan: Are these routing rules per-region? Our EU and US traffic need to stay in-region for compliance.
[07:12] Ethan: You can scope policies by region. For Private or VPC deployments you get region pinning and data residency controls. We also integrate with customer KMS for keys at rest.
[07:34] Maya: On KMS — we need HSM-level controls. Does Redwood support BYOK with HSM?

[07:50] Priya: Yes, BYOK via Cloud KMS or external HSMs for Private deployment. We'll include the security packet with the exact supported providers. Small note — the SOC-2 doc in the portal sometimes references "Samal" instead of SAML in auto-text, but it's SOC2 certified.
[08:20] Jordan: Good. Regarding observability, we want per-request token-level cost and latency. Can we drill down to individual replayable traces?
[08:36] Priya: Console has per-route token breakdown and a trace link when you enable tracing hooks. We also export to your tracing backend — jaeger, zipkin — and can stream audit logs to your SIEM.

[09:00] Ethan: Let's get into the demo scenario: payments auth service generating high QPS during peak. We'll show an org-level pool with protective floor for core services, and per-project keys for UX experiments that have lower guarantees.

[09:25] [screen: policy matrix visible] Priya: On this matrix you see 'core-payments' pinned to reserved capacity 200 qps, while 'checkout-experiments' lives in a shared burst pool. If core hits 80% we trigger auto-scale (if in Dedicated) or fallback routing in Hosted.
[09:55] Maya: If checkout-experiments saturates the shared pool, can core steal capacity?
[10:10] Priya: By default we enforce fairshare weights so core has higher weight; it will preempt less-weighted keys under contention. You can also set hard caps to totally prevent preemption.
[10:30] Jordan: How does preemption interact with long-running KV cache entries? We use KV cache heavily in our agents and don't want cold-starts.

[10:48] Priya: We keep KV caches warm per node and you can pin sticky sessions to nodes for keys. When preemption happens, traffic reroutes but we maintain cached artifacts where possible; sometimes there is a short warm-up.
[11:10] Ethan: Quick interject — customers sometimes see terminology mismatch between docs and Console — we'll send a short glossary mapping our UI terms to your infra concepts.
[11:25] Alvaro: Can you show the API side of configuring a quota programmatically? We want to automate provisioning when teams onboard.

[11:40] Priya: Yep, here's the API payload: you POST a policy with conditions and quota. Example: {"policy_name":"payments_floor","condition":{"org_id":"crescent-pay"},"quota":{"qps":200,"burst":500}} — small aside: the transcript may later have extra braces, but it's a straightforward REST call.
[12:10] [transcription artifact: braces shown in audio, might be cleaned up later]
[12:25] Jordan: Do you support concurrency quotas (tokens in-flight) vs QPS? We have expensive sync calls where concurrency is a better limiter.

[12:42] Priya: Yes they are separate controls. Concurrency limits are in-flight tokens and can be set per-key. We also expose throttle windows and per-route middleware hooks so you can handle backpressure gracefully.
[13:05] Maya: For billing attribution, can we tag by cost-center and have the usage exported to our billing system?
[13:20] Ethan: Yes tags propagate through the request lifecycle and export to billing reports. We'll send a sample export CSV format and a mapping guide.
[13:40] Alvaro: Security review — we need log retention for 12 months and export to Splunk. Is that doable?

[13:55] Priya: Absolutely; long retention is an Enterprise add-on. Audit logs can stream to your Splunk or S3 bucket with encryption. Note: the console UI labels 'audit' sometimes as 'audits' — tiny mismatch.
[14:20] Jordan: Any limitations we should know about with the hosted offering vs Private?

[14:32] Priya: Hosted is fastest to get started and supports region pinning and KMS integration for many needs; Private gives you full control — on-prem or VPC — plus deeper HSM/BYOK and network isolation. Throughput SLOs are better controlled in Dedicated reserved pools.
[14:55] Ethan: Now I'll simulate a spike — pushing 5x traffic from checkout-experiments — watch the dashboard metrics and the policy enforcement events.

[15:15] [demo noise] Priya: You can see the shared pool climbs and then the fairshare engine kicks in; 'core-payments' weight keeps latency stable while experiments get throttled with 429s and a Retry-After.
[15:40] Jordan: The 95th percentile latency stayed under 300ms for core — great. What about cost controls — can we set hard spend caps per org?
[15:58] Priya: Yes, budget caps are available; when you hit a cap we can block issuance of new tokens or switch to a cheaper model variant and alert your billing contacts.
[16:20] Alvaro: We run evals daily; will Redwood Optimize help identify quantization regressions or quality drift?
[16:35] Priya: Optimize can suggest quant profiles and flag eval regressions tied to prompt sets. It integrates with your CI to surface quality regressions pre-rollout.
[16:55] Jordan: For the pilot, we want 3 months, single-region US, 2 reserved slices for payments + a shared pool. Is that doable?
[17:10] Ethan: Totally, that's a common pilot. We'll propose a 3-month reserved config and a transition plan to Dedicated if you want guarantees.
[17:30] Maya: Any network requirements for VPC connectors? We have strict egress rules.
[17:45] Priya: Private deployments require specific subnets and route tables; we'll share the infra checklist. For hosted, we support private endpoints and peering in many clouds.
[18:05] [short mute for notes]
[18:20] Jordan: About SSO and RBAC — we need role separation for billing vs infra vs product. Does Console support fine-grained roles?
[18:37] Priya: Yes RBAC with SCIM provisioning, SAML SSO, and role templates. You can create custom roles for billing-only views.
[18:55] Alvaro: How are error budgets surfaced for teams? We want per-team SLA tracking.
[19:10] Ethan: Console has per-key SLA windows and an error budget dashboard; you can attach alerts when budget burn rate exceeds thresholds.
[19:30] Jordan: Can you briefly explain sticky routing — what if a node fails?

[19:45] Priya: Sticky routing pins keys to nodes for cache locality; if a node fails we rehydrate KV caches from persistent snapshot and migrate keys with minimal disruption — there can be a short tail latency spike.
[20:05] Maya: Any prebuilt Terraform or infra templates?
[20:18] Priya: Yes we have Terraform modules for key import, policy provisioning, and VPC connectors. We'll share the repo link in the follow-up.
[20:35] Jordan: Ok, can we run a short synthetic benchmark to validate your latency claims?
[20:50] Ethan: Absolutely. For pilots we often run a 24h synthetic run with your traffic profile. We'll coordinate with Maya for IP whitelisting.
[21:05] Alvaro: Quick thing — how does Redwood handle very low latency endpoints vs cost-sensitive batch embeddings?
[21:20] Priya: You can route latency-critical endpoints to Dedicated reserved slices and batch/embedding workloads to a different tier with larger batch sizes. Optimize suggests config for both.
[21:40] Jordan: Any caveats on model fallback for embeddings? We don't want quality regressions to go unnoticed.
[21:55] Priya: Fallbacks can be tied to eval gates — if fallback would degrade quality beyond threshold, we block automatic fallback and instead queue for review.
[22:10] [time jump in transcript — discussion continues with deep config examples]
[30:00] Priya: Showing API example for concurrency limit enforcement — you can set in-flight token limit and a bucket refill rate. The console visualizes token consumption in real-time.
[31:10] Jordan: Good. We also need to ensure logs are PII-sanitized — any built-in scrub rules?

[31:28] Priya: We have scrubbers that can redact patterns, and you can inject custom regexes during ingestion. That works for both hosted and private but for hosted we need to approve custom scrub rules for safety.
[32:00] Ethan: I know you folks care about procurement timing — what's your timeline Jordan?
[32:12] Jordan: We want to start pilot in mid-September and have production Q4 if results look good. Procurement will need the SOC2 and data processing addendum.
[32:30] Ethan: We'll send SOC2 + DPA and a sample contract clause. Priya will include the infra checklist and the policy examples.
[33:00] Maya: Can we limit the pilot to a test subnet egress and provide a static IP for your test runner?
[33:18] Priya: Yes, we can do whitelisted IPs or private peering. We'll coordinate the runner IPs before the benchmark.
[33:45] Alvaro: Any reference customers in fintech?
[33:58] Ethan: We have multiple finance customers — happy to share references under NDA. Some use cases are payments risk and customer verification.

[34:20] Jordan: Competitors conversation — we evaluated ModelServeX for on-prem but they lacked fairshare policy controls. OpenAI and Anthropic have API simplicity but not the org-level quota flexibility we need.
[34:50] Priya: Right — Redwood focuses on production economics and guardrails: predictable latency, cost controls, and routing policies across environments.
[35:10] [demo wrap-up screenshare stops]
[35:25] Priya: Quick recap of config artifacts we'll send: policy JSON examples, CSV template for key import, console screenshots, and the infra checklist.
[35:45] Ethan: And from AE side: pilot proposal and pricing. We'll propose 2 reserved slices + shared pool and a 3-month term.
[36:05] Jordan: Perfect. Any open risks we should call out?
[36:20] Priya: Main operational risks are cache warmup during large failovers and any custom scrub rules approval time. We'll list mitigations in the pilot plan.
[36:40] Maya: Anything else on RBAC/Scim?
[36:55] Priya: SCIM provisioning works with most IdPs; small note, some IdPs map groups differently and you'll need to map roles — we'll include a mapping example.
[37:15] Alvaro: Ok let's quickly run through next steps and owners so procurement can start.

[37:30] Ethan: Next steps summary: Priya sends technical pack (infra checklist, policy examples) by Friday; Ethan sends pricing and SOW draft by Monday; CrescentPay shares traffic profile and key list by next Wednesday; schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-09-10. Sound right?
[37:55] Jordan: Yes that's good. Also we need the SOC2 and DPA in the same email to legal.
[38:10] Ethan: Will do. We'll CC legal and procurement.
[38:25] [brief cross talk: laughter and thanks]
[38:40] Priya: Quick pro-tip — when you convert a key to reserved pool, the Console will show a 10-15min propagation window in Hosted; Dedicated is faster for reservations.
[39:00] Jordan: Noted. Any final questions from CrescentPay?
[39:10] Maya: No, just one thing — can the policy UI export to JSON for our CICD?
[39:22] Priya: Yes, export-to-JSON and Terraform modules available.
[39:35] Ethan: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts. If anything else comes up email me or book time on my calendar.
[39:50] Jordan: Thanks, much appreciated.
[40:05] Alvaro: Thanks all. End of call.
[52:10] [meeting end — recording stopped]
